site_name: Microsoft Fairwater Atlanta (inside the QTS Fayetteville campus, Georgia Highway 54, Fayetteville)
operator: Microsoft (facility sits inside a 615-acre campus developed by QTS)
load_basis: Epoch AI research estimate of IT power from satellite imagery with Buildings 1-2 operational (observation dated 2025-10-14, unchanged through 2026-05-15). Not an operator or utility figure. Epoch's 636 MW (our_load_mw) applies from 2026-06-14, when Buildings 3-4 are judged operational.
notes: UTILITY: Georgia Power, not Coweta-Fayette EMC, on three sources that all concern the QTS Fayetteville campus (the AJC, 2025-11-21, places the Microsoft facility inside that QTS campus: https://www.ajc.com/business/2025/11/microsofts-newest-ai-superfactory-opens-at-sprawling-fayetteville-campus). (1) Georgia PSC Docket 44280, Southern Environmental Law Center motion filed 2025-01-10, attaches a page of Georgia Power's own transmission ten-year plan titled 'CC - QTS FAYETTEVILLE TRANSMISSION NEEDS' (CC = customer choice): a new Ashley Park 500/230 kV substation and two ~6-mile 230 kV lines 'to the high side of customer substations', need date 04/01/2026. The motion states 'Georgia Power made QTS an offer' and reads Georgia Power's August 2024 letter to residents as 'implying that QTS had previously signed a contract for service'. (2) WSB-TV, 2024-07-08: 'In order to power this facility, Georgia Power will have to expand power lines in the area' (https://www.wsbtv.com/news/local/fayette-county/new-data-center-is-coming-fayette-county-neighbors-dont-want-power-poles-it-needs/FTMLDK6URNEJRDFRK2EWB7G6IA/). (3) A resident letter in The Citizen, 2024-04-29, says Georgia Power was buying easements for a 230 kV line 'for the QTS Data Center'. Confidence is medium rather than high because no retrieved document states the retail supply contract outright; the contract is an inference drawn by the SELC filing, and no source addresses the Microsoft building separately from the QTS campus. ARRANGEMENT: special_contract = a negotiated customer-choice offer under Georgia's Territorial Electric Service Act (large new loads pick a supplier once), per the same PSC filing; contract terms are not public and none were collected. YEAR: Microsoft says the Atlanta site 'began operation in October' (article dated 2025-11-12); AJC confirms. LOAD: no operator or utility MW figure exists in the sources read. The PSC filing cites trade press that two buildings on the QTS campus would draw 340 MW, and gives the filer's own rough estimate of about 1,320 MW for the full 6.6M sq ft QTS campus; planned_full_buildout_mw = 636 is Epoch's figure for the Microsoft Fairwater buildings only, not the QTS campus. County from AJC. lat/lon left null per the output spec.

site_name: Amazon (AWS) Hilliard data center campus, 4600 Cosgray Rd (permit name CMH091 Campus)
notes: UTILITY: AEP Ohio (Ohio Power Company), not Columbus Division of Power. City of Hilliard's fuel-cell FAQ: a 72.9 MW solid-oxide fuel cell plant at 4186 Scioto Darby Creek Road, 'within Amazon's 142-acre data-center campus', will be 'constructed, owned, and operated by Ohio Power Company (AEP Ohio)', will 'operate behind the meter', and exists because 'AEP has indicated that it does not have sufficient electrical capacity to service all of the planned data center buildings' on the campus. Ohio Power Siting Board approved it 2025-09-22 (case 25-0649-EL-BLN); operation projected September 2027. Signal Ohio quotes Amazon that AEP 'will temporarily use fuel cells to power part of our data center operations' (https://signalohio.org/columbus-suburb-sues-to-block-amazon-data-centers-six-acre-array-of-228-fuel-cells-ohio). Confidence is medium, not high: the sources tie AEP Ohio to Amazon's 142-acre Hilliard campus by its Scioto Darby Creek Road address, and I could not confirm from a primary record that 4600 Cosgray Rd is the same campus rather than the adjoining one (the two roads intersect; press accounts differ on which Hilliard campus gets the fuel cells). AEP Ohio is the utility for Amazon's Hilliard campuses in every source read, and none mentions the City of Columbus utility. ARRANGEMENT: left unknown for the study period. Grid supply through 2025 comes from AEP Ohio on terms not established here. From about 2027 part of the load would be behind-the-meter fuel cells owned by AEP Ohio under a private agreement paid for by Amazon (special contract plus behind the meter). A search result title pointed to a 2024 AEP-Amazon arrangement document; it was not opened, to stay blind to rate terms. YEAR NOT FOUND in an acceptable source. FireRescue1 says the Hilliard campus next to the fuel-cell site was approved in 2022; Signal Ohio calls it 'already-built' with a 'recently built' fleet of 158 backup diesel generators. Directory sites give 2022 and 2024 for the Cosgray buildings (not usable, and they disagree). Our 2023 is neither confirmed nor contradicted. LOAD NOT FOUND: no MW figure for the campus; the 73 MW is the fuel-cell plant only. County is standard geography for Hilliard, not from a fetched record. Axios returned 403 and was not read. lat/lon left null per the output spec.

site_name: CyrusOne Houston West campus (11003 Corporate Centre Dr; operator lists the campus as HOU3-HOU4)
load_basis: Operator page: 84 MW total IT capacity for the Houston HOU3-HOU4 campus (HOU3 174,000 sq ft and HOU4 173,000 sq ft of technical space; 68 diesel generators of 2,250 kW each). Built IT capacity, not metered load. The page gives no street address, so the match to this parcel is by it being the operator's only listed Houston campus.
notes: SERVING UTILITY NOT FOUND in an acceptable source. Trade press and the operator say only 'redundant utility power feeds'; an SEC full-text search for CyrusOne with CenterPoint and Houston West returned nothing. Our Entergy Texas assignment is very likely wrong for a west Houston address inside Beltway 8. UNVERIFIED LEAD (territory knowledge, no document): CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric is the wires utility here, in ERCOT's competitive retail area, so the energy seller would be a retail electric provider chosen by the customer and the bill-relevant delivery utility would be CenterPoint. YEAR: low confidence because it depends on which building the parcel is. Bisnow, 2015-12-04, reports CyrusOne 'has opened its third Houston West campus facility' (Houston West III); listings place Houston West III at 11003 Corporate Centre Dr, while Bisnow gives the campus address 5150 Westway Park Blvd. The campus itself is older: Data Center Knowledge, 2009-12-17, reports the first 94,000 sq ft Houston West building 'fully commissioned and ready for customer installation' (https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/operations-and-management/cyrusone-opens-new-houston-data-center). Use 2009 if the unit of analysis is the campus, 2015 for this building. Either way our 2024 reflects only the 2023 'West Campus Expansion' generator permit, not first energization. LOAD: our 132.1 MW exceeds the operator's 84 MW IT figure. Data Center Knowledge, 2014-04-18, gave Houston West III 'up to 96 megawatts of critical load upon completion' as a design ceiling; not recorded as planned buildout because the operator's current page supersedes it and no current full-build figure is published. County is standard geography. DataCenterDynamics and GlobeSt returned 403 and were not read. lat/lon left null per the output spec.

notes: UTILITY: trade-press report of NTT's 2020-02-11 announcement quotes 'Portland General Electric (PGE) will supply power to the campus'. This upgrades round 1, which had PGE from a directory only. The NTT newsroom original now returns 404; the Lightwave copy is cited. ARRANGEMENT: recorded as retail because the operator says PGE supplies the power; the tariff or any contract, and whether the site later moved to direct access, were not looked up. YEAR NOT CONFIRMED: the February 2020 announcement expected 'the first 6 MW of critical IT load' by mid-2020, which is an expectation, not a record of operation. The operator's HI1 page gives no opening date. Our 2021 (2020 generator permit plus one) is plausible and uncontradicted, but the only source stating 2021 is a directory. LOAD: our 92.6 MW is well above the operator's 36 MW for the only completed building. Planned buildout is 126 MW per the operator's current page; the 2020 announcement said five buildings totalling 144 MW. County is standard geography for Hillsboro. lat/lon left null per the output spec.

site_name: Amazon data center campus, 75242 Gar Swanson Rd, Boardman
notes: UTILITY: La Grande Observer, 2023-04-11 ('Amazon strikes power deal for data centers'), identifies Umatilla Electric Cooperative as 'the local power utility' for Amazon's data centers near Boardman and Hermiston and says Amazon 'started working with the local power utility, Umatilla Electric Cooperative, to choose the electricity supply'. This is a fleet-level statement about Amazon's Boardman campuses, not one that names the Gar Swanson Road address, hence medium rather than high. The only other mapped candidate, Bonneville Power Administration, is a wholesale supplier to the co-op, not a retail alternative. This upgrades round 1, which had UEC only as an inference from UEC substation projects. ARRANGEMENT: recorded as special_contract on the strength of that article: UEC delivers, and Amazon selects the power supply through an arrangement with the co-op rather than taking the co-op's standard supply. The article notes UEC did not answer questions about the arrangement, so its terms and start date are not established, and it may not have applied before 2023. YEAR NOT FOUND for this campus. The same article says Amazon had operated data centers in eastern Oregon for about a dozen years as of 2023 (so since about 2011), which is the first Port of Morrow campus, not this one. Our 2022 rests only on the 2021 generator permit. LOAD NOT FOUND; our 84.9 MW is unverified. County is standard geography for Boardman. Idaho Capital Sun returned 403 and was not read. lat/lon left null per the output spec.

site_name: Microsoft data center, 608 Ridge Road, Boydton (permit name Timber Datacenter)
serving_utility: Dominion Energy Virginia (Virginia Electric & Power Co)
notes: UTILITY IS A LOW-CONFIDENCE INFERENCE, not a site-specific finding, and it runs against our Mecklenburg Electric Cooperative assignment. Evidence: (1) Data Center Knowledge, 2010-08-27, on Microsoft's original Boydton site: 'The site is served by Dominion Virginia Power'. That is the first campus, not the 608 Ridge Road parcel. (2) Dominion's own project pages show a run of 230 kV builds in Mecklenburg County for this load: Butler Farm (SCC case PUR-2022-00175, approved 2023-05-31, 'customer substation site', Chase City area, target completion end of 2026: https://www.dominionenergy.com/about/delivering-energy/electric-projects/power-line-projects/butler-farm), Jeffress (PUR-2023-00088, approved 2024-01-16), and Nebula-Raines (PUR-2025-00014, approved 2025-10-03, linking 'the Chase City/Boydton area' to South Hill). None of the pages read names Microsoft or Ridge Road. (3) Lead not opened (Virginia Business returned 403; seen only as a search-result summary): as of summer 2025 Mecklenburg Electric Cooperative reportedly had a single member of 5 MW or more, and a Clarksville operator (TECfusions) identified itself as that member. If accurate, no Microsoft campus was a co-op member then. (4) Old Dominion Electric Cooperative's FY2025 Form 10-K lists Mecklenburg Electric Cooperative as a member and discusses data-center load across its members without naming Microsoft or attributing any to Mecklenburg (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/885568/000119312526110107/ck0000885568-20251231.htm). Nothing retrieved ties this specific parcel to either utility, so serving_utility_matches_ours=false should be treated as probable, not settled. The SCC dockets above are the place to confirm which Dominion substation sits on the Ridge Road site. YEAR AND LOAD NOT FOUND. Microsoft's October 2025 Virginia fact sheet says only that it operates and is building datacenters in Mecklenburg County. Our 2024 and 82.1 MW are unverified. County is standard geography for Boydton. lat/lon left null per the output spec.
